audience: Oslo skincare buyers who follow ingredient-led routines and buy premium serums online.

copy_lines.text: Ny serum. Ekte hud, ekte resultater.

hypothesis: An AI-made creative set can reach the 90-order goal inside budget, because the human route needs 36 extra orders to break even, 40 percent of the goal, which premium serum launches rarely add.
insight: Shoppers judge a new serum on proof and provenance, not polish; a believable result beats a glossy studio image.

maker_recommendation.rationale: Decide puts break-even at 36 of the 90 goal orders, 40 percent of the goal, so the studio shoot only pays back if it lifts orders beyond that; at 2500 kr per order the AI route carries far less downside.

mandatories.text: Ads where a person's body shape, size or skin has been altered must carry the 'retusjert reklame' label (markedsforingsloven par. 2). AI-altered images of real people are in scope.
If the campaign also reaches EU audiences, realistic AI-made people, places or products that could pass as real must be visibly labelled as AI (EU AI Act Article 50).
AI-generated creative is disclosed to the client and labelled to the audience where a reasonable viewer could take it for an unedited photograph of a real person.

objective: Launch Aurora Atelier's new serum line in Oslo and win 90 first orders within the campaign window.
open_questions: What is the account's real conversion rate and CPM, which would replace the assumed 2500 kr value per order?
Does the Oslo launch also reach EU audiences, which would trigger AI Act labelling?
